title: Bet Dwarka - The Sacred Island of Lord Krishna
content:
Beyt Dwarka Island

Located about 30 km from Dwarka city, Beyt Dwarka Island (also known as Bet Dwarka) is a serene and spiritually significant island off the coast of Gujarat. Believed to be the original residence of Lord Krishna, the island holds immense religious importance and attracts thousands of pilgrims and tourists every year. Surrounded by the crystal-clear waters of the Arabian Sea, Beyt Dwarka offers a blend of spirituality, natural beauty, and cultural heritage.

According to Hindu mythology, this is where Lord Krishna lived with his family after moving from Mathura. The island is home to the Beyt Dwarkadhish Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna and believed to have been built by his devotee, Vajranabh - the grandson of Krishna. The temple’s architecture reflects the charm of old coastal Gujarat, with intricate carvings, small shrines, and the sound of conch shells creating a truly divine atmosphere.

Besides its spiritual significance, Beyt Dwarka also offers pristine beaches, snorkeling, and opportunities to witness marine life, including dolphins and sea turtles. The island’s calm environment, combined with its mythological connection, makes it a perfect destination for pilgrims and travelers seeking peace and beauty.

Location

State: Gujarat, India

District: Devbhoomi Dwarka

Distance from Dwarka: Around 30 km

Access: Reachable via ferry from Okha Port

How to Reach Bet Dwarka

  • By Road: Reach Okha, about 30 km from Dwarka, via taxi or local bus.
  • By Ferry: Take a ferry boat from Okha Jetty to Bet Dwarka (15-20 minutes ride). Boats operate regularly from morning till evening.
  • By Rail: Nearest railway station is Okha Station (approx. 1 km from jetty).
  • By Air: Nearest airport is Jamnagar (around 140 km away).

Religious Significance

Bet Dwarka is believed to be the original residential place of Lord Krishna, where he lived with his family. The name “Bet” means “gift”, and the place is said to have been gifted to Krishna by his devotee Sudama.

The main temple on the island is Shrine of Lord Krishna, often associated with Dwarakadheesh form of Krishna. The temple is over 500 years old and was believed to be built by Vallabhacharya.

Main Attractions at Bet Dwarka

1. Shri Krishna Temple - Houses an idol of Krishna that resembles the one in Dwarkadhish Temple. Entry is free, and non-commercialized, maintaining a peaceful spiritual vibe. Special prayers during Janmashtami and Diwali.

2. Hanuman Dandi Temple - Dedicated to Hanuman and his son Makardhwaja. One of the few temples with Makardhwaja as the deity.

3. Rukmini Temple - A small temple for Rukmini Devi, Krishna’s consort. Peaceful and located near the beach.

4. Gufa Mandir (Cave Temple) - Underground shrine said to be the meditative place of Lord Krishna.

Scenic Beauty & Spiritual Vibes

Besides being a spiritual destination, Bet Dwarka is also known for: Pristine beaches, Clean and peaceful surroundings, Beautiful sea views and Shell collecting and coastal exploration.

You can enjoy a peaceful walk along the beach after visiting the temples, making it a great mix of spirituality and nature.

Timings

  • Ferry Service: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM (subject to weather and tide)
  • Temple Timings: 6:00 AM - 1:00 PM & 3:00 PM - 8:00 PM

Best Time to Visit

The ideal time to visit Bet Dwarka is October to March, when the weather is pleasant. Avoid monsoon season (July-September) as ferry services may be disrupted due to high tides.

Travel Tips

  • Carry cash - Bet Dwarka has limited ATM or card facilities.
  • Wear modest and comfortable clothes suitable for temples.
  • Footwear is not allowed inside the temple, so be prepared to walk barefoot.
  • Boats can get crowded during festivals and holidays - arrive early.
  • Keep water bottles and sun protection, especially during warmer months.

faqs.question: Is photography allowed in Bet Dwarka Temple?
faqs.answer: Photography is not allowed inside the main Krishna Temple at Bet Dwarka. However, you can take photos outside the temple and around the island.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Bet Dwarka?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Bet Dwarka is from October to March, when the weather is cooler and suitable for travel. Avoid monsoon months (July–September) due to rough seas and possible ferry disruptions.

faqs.question: What are the ferry timings to Bet Dwarka?
faqs.answer: Ferry services to Bet Dwarka usually operate between 6:00 AM and 6:00 PM, depending on weather and sea conditions. It’s best to reach early during peak seasons or festivals.

faqs.question: How can I reach Bet Dwarka from Dwarka?
faqs.answer: To reach Bet Dwarka from Dwarka, travel to Okha Port (around 30 km by road), then take a ferry to the island. Ferries run regularly from morning to evening and the ride takes about 15-20 minutes.

faqs.question: What should I wear when visiting Bet Dwarka Temple?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to wear modest and traditional clothing, suitable for temple visits. Footwear must be removed before entering the temple premises.
